description: For a Cape Town switching substation (33/66/132kV), at 06:00 SAST on day D, will the evening peak load (maximum half-hourly MVA over 16:00-22:00 SAST) exceed the station's trailing-90-evening p95 (minimum 30 prior evenings)? Features are the station identity, the calendar, the same-day 00:00-06:00 half-hourly readings and the mean of the trailing <= 90 prior days' morning peaks. No evening-derived value ships: evening readings, evening peaks and the trailing-evening p95 threshold are sealed outside the artifact (a sliding evening quantile's day-over-day delta reconstructs labels - the fts-appeal-003 P0 lesson), so the model predicts exceedance of a threshold it never sees. A useful prediction at 06:00 lets the distribution desk flag evenings that will stress a substation before the evening ramp, in a city whose publisher notes readings are not corrected for load shifts.
name: za-cct-substation-evening-peak-exceedance
positive_label_text: evening peak (max half-hourly MVA over 16:00-22:00 SAST) exceeds the station's trailing-90-evening p95
split: temporal on the target day: train 2022, eval 2023, holdout 2024
split_description: temporal on the target day (Africa/Johannesburg): train 2022, eval 2023, holdout 2024; the first 30 days of each station's series are burn-in (no 30 prior evenings for the p95) and are excluded, counted, never scored
